To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Daxx and/or ATRX regulate transcription and histone H3 assembly at a chromatin template.

(1) Daxx and its partner, ATRX, are required for the maintenance of a repressed chromosomal environment; (2) Daxx-ATRX-dependent chromatin assembly is required for transcription repression; and (3) Daxx is required for the maintenance and recruitment of PML-NBs at the transgene array.
the DaxX and ATRX chromatin pathway regulates replication-independent histone incorporation at a transcriptionally repressed inducible transgen array.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of gene expression regulation.
understanding how the PML-NB/Nuclear Domain 10 protein, Daxx, regulates gene expression, and how this relates to its role in viral infection.
the mechanisms through which Daxx/Atrx regulate transcriptional repression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Daxx and its partner ATRX are important regulators of transcriptional silencing and chromatin assembly and that this is likely to be a function of their ability to regulate histone H3 variant exchange.

Daxx and its associated proteins, such as PML and ATRX form a complex that regulates the chromatin environment at specific loci in the genome, such as the array used here, and that this complex is required for chromatin assembly at these loci.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that Daxx and the PML-NB protein ATRX are important regulators of transcriptional repression and that this repression is mediated through their ability to regulate replication-independent chromatin assembly.
the PML-NB-associated Daxx and/or ATRX pathway regulates replication-independent histone deposition and transcriptional silencing by blocking chromatin assembly at sites of gene repression.
we have used a transgene array to study the mechanism by which PML-NBs repress transcription and prevent viral activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Daxx and the ATRX chromatin remodelling factor are required to maintain chromatin in a repressed state and that histone deposition is blocked when transcription is initiated.
ATRX and its partner Daxx are essential for maintaining a chromatin environment that represses transcription.
Daxx and its binding partner, the chromatin remodeller ATRX, are required to maintain transcriptional repression and to block histone H3 chromatin assembly.
